title: Звонок из больницы  (The Call from the Hospital)

segments.t: Resting in a hospital ward after having his stomach pumped, Max panics when his phone rings and asks his hospital roommate to pretend to be a doctor and say Max wandered off. Seconds later, Max takes the phone back and realizes that the caller was actually Sasha, while he still needs an excuse for Vika.
У меня для вас плохие новости.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Hello, good afternoon.' Notice how Russian expresses 'hello' and 'hello' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
'He cannot come to the phone right now.' In Russian, the idea of 'any minute' flows naturally into 'to walk up to' without extra filler words.
'Hello, I am a friend of his.' In Russian, the idea of 'hello' flows naturally into 'friend' without extra filler words.
'Oh, it is good that you called.' The meaning hinges on 'about' working together with 'called' in spoken Russian. Vika answers right away.
У меня для вас плохие новости.
'I have bad news for you.' In Russian, the idea of 'by' flows naturally into 'news' without extra filler words.
'We lost him.' Nastya anchors the line on 'we', while 'lost' completes the thought.
'He walked out into the hallway and disappeared somewhere.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'to go out' places the action in the masculine past tense. Vika answers right away.
'Now we cannot find him anywhere.' The grammar packs 'now' and 'find' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Wait a second, so he is alive?' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'wait' and 'like this' in a few short words.
'Listen, was that you playing a prank?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Max's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
'Well, where are you?' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'where' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'It looks like I ate something bad.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'to sit down' to negate the statement.

'So here I am lying down and resting.' The grammar packs 'there you go' and 'am resting' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
У меня для вас плохие новости.

That wraps up this scene as taken to the hospital with food poisoning, Max has a fellow patient tell Vika on the phone that he went missing, only to realize he accidentally pulled the prank on Sasha instead. Until next time!
